narrator.instructions: Warm, confident corporate trainer speaking American English to colleagues. Clear, friendly, professional; natural conversational pace, brief pauses between list items. Never robotic.

exec.instructions: Speak American English. Senior executive; composed, low and confident.

mentor.instructions: Speak American English. Calm, friendly expert; warm, clear, a touch of dry humour.

rookie.instructions: Speak American English. Good-natured, over-eager new starter; expressive, quick to panic, comic.

vex.instructions: Speak American English. Smug, theatrical cartoon con-artist, playful not scary. Savouring every word.

narration.text: Spot the signs. ^ It's not Hana's usual address. ^ It says pay today. ^ The bank details are new. ^ And it asks for secrecy.

claims.text: Warning sign: a sender address or reply-to address that does not match the usual one.

Report suspicious payment requests to IT Security with the Report Phishing button in Outlook or the IT Security hotline on extension 4400.

nodes.feedback: You paid on an unverified email. Urgency, new bank details and secrecy were the red flags. Call back a known number, and if money has gone, report it to IT Security and Finance at once.
